 Josh Giddey had 15 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), 10 rebounds, 14 assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Giddey’s triple-double was his first of the season and his 21st since joining the Bulls. Only Michael Jordan (28) has more in franchise history. Giddey has made at least 44 percent of his attempts in four consecutive games after an early season shooting slump. He and the Bulls will face the Timberwolves on Saturday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 The Bulls will start Josh Giddey, Norman Powell, Isaac Okoro, Matas Buzelis, and Jalen Smith against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Caleb Wilson (hand) will be out for at least four weeks which is why he’s not in the starting lineup. Isaac Okoro will move to the small forward position as Norman Powell (back) returns to play. Okoro could still be used a streamer in redraft leagues, but the upside isn’t the highest. 
 Josh Giddey 
 CHI 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Josh Giddey produced 19 points (7-of-12 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, 15 assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers. 
 Despite the outcome, this was Giddey’s best performance of the season. Scoring in double figures for the sixth straight game, he recorded season highs in points and assists against the 76ers. Given how poorly Giddey has shot the ball, his making over half his attempts on Sunday was a welcome step in the right direction. The Bulls play three games next week, starting with the Spurs on Wednesday. 
 Josh Giddey 
 CHI 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Josh Giddey finished Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks with 10 points (4-of-7 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), one rebound, six assists and one three-pointer. 
 After a rough first three games to begin the season, Giddey has shot 50 percent or better from the field in three of his last five outings. The final line against the Knicks wasn’t great, but at least category-league managers didn’t take a hit in the field-goal percentage category. 
 Josh Giddey 
 CHI 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Josh Giddey posted a double-double on Monday with 13 points (5-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, 10 assists, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers against the 76ers. 
 Giddey’s scoring struggles continued in this game, but when he has played at least 25 minutes in a game this season, he has dished out at least 10 assists. That trend continued in this game, which ended up being one of his better performances this season. Giddey certainly hasn’t played to his ADP to this point of the year, but outings like this one will certainly help redeem his value. 
 Tre Jones 
 CHI 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Tre Jones finished Friday’s loss to the Celtics with 12 points (4-of-10 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, four steals and one block. 
 In his usual role backing up Josh Giddey (13/4/5 with two three-pointers), Jones played 20 minutes on Friday. That didn’t prevent him from providing solid category-league value, especially in steals. The four pilfers were one shy of his career-high, and the Bulls guard also managed to block a shot. Regardless of what Giddey does on any given night, Jones is worth rostering in deep leagues. 
 Josh Giddey 
 CHI 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Josh Giddey finished Monday’s loss to the Celtics with 11 points (4-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, four assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer. 
 After shooting a combined 7-of-26 from the field in Chicago’s first three games, Giddey was more accurate on Monday. Unfortunately for him and the Bulls, that didn’t keep them from getting blown out in Boston. Overall, Giddey’s final stat line wasn’t great, but those rostering him can’t ignore that he shot better than in Week 1. 
 Josh Giddey 
 CHI 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Josh Giddey accounted for nine points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Wizards. 
 After shooting a combined 4-of-19 from the field in Chicago’s first two games, Giddey was considerably better on Saturday. Although he finished with just nine points, fantasy managers will be pleased with his rebounds and assists. Over three games, Giddey has shot 26.9 percent from the field and 50.0 percent from the foul line, numbers that must improve if he’s to justify his second-round ADP from the preseason.

 Josh Giddey (wrist) is available for Friday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Giddey is good to go after being listed as probable on the Bulls’ initial injury report. He’ll take on his usual role as starting point guard, so managers rostering Giddey need to ensure he’s in their lineups before the 4 PM Eastern start time.

 Josh Giddey (wrist) is probable for Friday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Giddey, who struggled mightily in Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors, is dealing with a sprained left wrist. However, the probable tag suggests he’ll fill his usual starting point guard role. If Giddey can’t play, Tre Jones is the most likely replacement. 
 Josh Giddey 
 CHI 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Josh Giddey produced two points (1-of-10 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds and six assists in Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors. 
 None of the Bulls played particularly well in Wednesday’s 135-92 defeat, so this result can’t be pinned on Giddey alone. The concern for fantasy managers is that his cold shooting in the preseason carried over into Wednesday’s season opener. The hope is that Giddey will bounce back on Friday when the Bulls visit the Bucks, who are also rebuilding.
